attempts.summary: Established an AIDE-based file integrity baseline for /etc on node1 (Ubuntu 16.04). Installed aide/aide-common, confirmed the distro's default config already covers /etc recursively via a catch-all '/ Full' rule (excluding /proc, /sys) plus curated per-package rules, and added an explicit '/etc Full' fragment for clarity. Built and installed the baseline database at /var/lib/aide/aide.db (70,163 entries) with creation timestamp and sha256 recorded under /var/lib/aide/baseline-meta/. Verified change detection by creating a test file under /etc, confirming aide --check flagged it as added, then removing it and confirming a clean state. Completed the mandatory single-node restart protocol: captured pre-restart boot_id and healthy baseline state, issued a native reboot, polled until SSH returned, proved boot_id changed, and confirmed post-restart that the baseline database was byte-identical (same sha256), /etc still matched the baseline, and change detection still worked correctly.
